title: `sort`: NULLs first, ascending and descending
description: `sort` puts NULLs first by default, ascending and descending; `nulls_last=True` puts them last, per key when given a list. So Polars's default is the same NULL placement in both directions, where SQL's convention flips it with the direction.
reference: The key's direction states the NULL placement; `SORT_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED` is `NULLS_LAST` (D8). Polars is native for every stated direction with `nulls_last`; its default differs from DuckDB's `NULLS_LAST` (duckdb-F2).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
